attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Try the root-only algorithm that killed H018.
attacks.method: Check all coverage and two-sided decision clauses.
attacks.notes: The repaired formulation explicitly forbids the vacuous construction.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Hide SAT solving inside canonical representative computation.
attacks.method: Require a fixed certificate language and charge all canonicalization time.
attacks.notes: The loophole is syntactically closed, though no canonicalizer is known.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Encode an arbitrary subfunction as one interface symbol.
attacks.method: Enforce finite fan-in-two gates and count every node recursively.
attacks.notes: The repaired language blocks unit-cost global functions.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Translate the interface DAG to DNNF and invoke exponential lower bounds.
attacks.method: Test whether elimination certificates guarantee decomposability or determinism.
attacks.notes: No polynomial translation for the exact interface language has been established; H050 isolates this attack.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Use Tseitin contradictions as hard instances.
attacks.method: Apply Gaussian elimination to the entire affine core.
attacks.notes: Pure parity instances are intentionally easy and cannot refute the conjecture.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Hide arbitrary CNF reasoning in unrestricted cardinality constraints.
attacks.method: Require polynomially solvable explicit cardinality forms and charge encoding length.
attacks.notes: The exact allowed cardinality language must be fixed before formalization.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Let the transformer solve SAT before outputting a constant function.
attacks.method: Forbid arbitrary computation by fixing the grammar and local certificates.
attacks.notes: The broad circular loophole is closed by the finite grammar.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Use valued-CSP classifications to show local submodular gadgets cannot express all Boolean relations.
attacks.method: Audit whether auxiliary minimization and rational weights fall inside an existing closure theorem.
attacks.notes: This is a promising refutation route, but no exact theorem was registered for the full grammar model.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Apply exponential correlation-polytope extension complexity directly.
attacks.method: Check whether the hypothesis encodes only nonemptiness and witness recovery rather than the full satisfying-assignment polytope.
attacks.notes: Standard polytope lower bounds do not automatically apply to nonemptiness-only lifts.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Prove finite TU gadgets preserve a tractable relational clone.
attacks.method: Compare projections and shared auxiliaries with known TU closure properties.
attacks.notes: No exact closure theorem covering the stated grammar has been supplied.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Invoke known constant-level SoS gaps for random CSPs.
attacks.method: Check whether the gaps survive the exact finite extension grammar and extraction requirement.
attacks.notes: Existing gaps are highly relevant but were not shown closed under every allowed local extension.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Hide exponential complexity in the base polynomial degrees or coefficients.
attacks.method: Bound total encoding length, coefficient bits, and grammar scope.
attacks.notes: The formulation charges these resources explicitly.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Note that polynomially bounded proofs need not be findable efficiently.
attacks.method: The hypothesis explicitly requires a search algorithm, so use this as a plausibility attack rather than a logical contradiction.
attacks.notes: It is strictly stronger than H025 and cannot inherit proof existence evidence.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Show that verifying unrestricted circuit identities is not deterministically known in P.
attacks.method: Require sparse multilinear line representations or a certified restricted identity class.
attacks.notes: The exact representation/verifier pair remains the next formalization gate.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Remove the tractable-residual clause and observe that isolation does not decide existence.
attacks.method: Verify that the statement includes a deterministic solver and recovery for every isolated residual.
attacks.notes: The previously fatal omission is repaired.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Argue that known isolation is randomized and may require many random hashes.
attacks.method: Treat this as the exact missing derandomization gate.
attacks.notes: No deterministic universal family with the full residual promise is known.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Short resolution proofs may exist while a fixed CDCL policy takes exponential time.
attacks.method: Search candidate pebbling, guarded, and random formulas under the exact scheduler.
attacks.notes: This is the leading computational refutation route, but no universal counterfamily is yet recorded.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Choose branches using a SAT oracle.
attacks.method: Require the branching rule to be a fixed polynomial-time function of the current trail and database.
attacks.notes: The formulation blocks oracle branching.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Observe that #SAT has only O(n) output bits, so output size itself is not an obstruction.
attacks.method: Audit intermediate integer bit growth and circuit evaluation cost instead.
attacks.notes: Polynomial bit length remains possible in principle.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Transfer DNNF lower bounds to the arithmetic DAG.
attacks.method: Check whether subtraction and cancellation invalidate monotone compilation lower bounds.
attacks.notes: The signed arithmetic language may evade direct DNNF bounds, requiring a stronger invariant.
